title: Fruit Trees furnishing fabric
lede: Alexander Girard turns trees into symmetrical black stems hung with flat orange, pink, and olive circles, ovals, and squares on white cotton.
summary: Symmetrical black-stemmed trees with flat orange, pink, and olive fruit shapes in vertical repeats. Alexander Girard for Herman Miller, 1960.

source.label: Art Institute of Chicago: Fruit Trees (Furnishing Fabric), 1988.76

evidence.note: Inspected, in the scratchpad only, the Art Institute of Chicago image of 1988.76 at 843 × 574 px (the largest size the museum serves for this in-copyright object). The image shows a detail with four vertical repeats. Not stored.

styles.note: Flat geometric fruit and plant forms, a warm orange-pink-olive palette on white, and folk-derived pattern: Girard’s Herman Miller textiles are a core source for the style.

context: The Art Institute of Chicago dates the fabric 1960 and describes it as cotton, plain weave, screen printed; designed by Alexander Girard (1907–1993) and produced by Herman Miller, Inc., Zeeland, Michigan. The piece measures 104 × 132.5 cm with a repeat of 58.8 × 30.8 cm. Credit line: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Alexander Girard; Alexander Demond Fund. [AIC 1988.76](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/71159/fruit-trees-furnishing-fabric).
The museum’s API marks the object as not public domain.
observed: The ground is white. Black stems branch symmetrically from a central trunk in each repeat, with small curled tips.
Fruit shapes hang from the branches: orange and pink circles, pale pink ovals, orange and pink squares and trapezoids, and olive-green ovals on the trunk.
The shapes are flat color with no outlines; the black line is only the stems.
The trees stand in vertical columns side by side, with narrow white gaps between them.
interpretation: Girard mixes circles and squares freely on a folk-like tree form. The palette is warm and saturated, but softened by the pale pink and the white ground.
This is the “pattern as a band” idea at textile scale: small flat shapes repeated in columns.
borrow: Build a symmetric plant from a thin black stem and flat, unoutlined circles, ovals, and squares.
Use orange, pale pink, and olive together on white for a warm but light repeat.

rights.statement: No image is stored. Alexander Girard died in 1993; the Art Institute of Chicago does not mark the object as public domain.
